title: transient-circuit-thaw-and-tenant-restore
author: Marta Novak
description: Context: In the last month we've observed a recurring class of incidents where regional failovers or tenant-level eviction cause 'sticky' circuit states: a tenant remains in a degraded/locked circuit for multiple minutes after the primary capacity returns. Symptoms: elevated 5xx rates on soft-degraded routes, manual operator intervention to clear circuit cache, and surprise latency spikes during tenant reinstatement. Root cause analysis traced the issue to an interplay between the circuit-state ttl and the tenant-provisioned backoff that prevented the circuit manager from performing a short thaw when upstream capacity reclaimed. Motivation: reduce time-to-recovery for tenants stuck in soft-degradation without risking flapping or unsafe reopen of critical routes. This PR introduces a safe, observable "transient thaw" mechanism, plus a small operator-facing endpoint and telemetry to make incidents recover automatically and auditable.

1) Initialize transient thaw window in circuit-manager (feat): 0a7b3e6
2) Add idempotent /admin/circuit/thaw endpoint (chore): 9c3f1d2
3) Emit circuit_thaw events to audit log and metrics (feat): f4b2a11

files_changed: src/circuit/circuit_manager.rs, src/circuit/thaw_controller.rs, src/http/admin_routes.rs, telemetry/metrics.toml, tests/integration/circuit_thaw.rs, docs/ops/circuit-thaw.md, deployment/helm/values.yaml
review_comments:
Aisha Patel: Please ensure the transient thaw respects tenant-level SLO weights; we can't unilaterally reopen heavy tenants during global pressure. Suggested: add a check in thaw_controller that consults tenant_slo_weight and aborts if > 0.9.
Diego Ramos: Integration tests look solid; ask to make the /admin endpoint require a KMS-signed token or operator role. Also flagged potential race in cache eviction path.
Liang Chen: Can we emit a circuit_thaw_audit.trace_id for correlation with request traces? That would help postmortems.

Author replies:
Marta Novak: Added tenant_slo_weight guard (see thaw_controller.rs) and tied the endpoint to existing operator auth middleware (admin token check). Emitted circuit_thaw.trace_id and added test assertions. Addressed race by switching cache removal to an atomic compare-and-swap path and added retry with jitter.
Diego Ramos: Approved after small follow-up to make metric names stable.
Aisha Patel: Approved; left a note in docs about when operators should avoid manual thaw to prevent flapping.
ci_summary: CI pipeline: build: pass; unit-tests: pass; integration-tests: flaky first run (1 failing timing test) -> rerun -> pass; e2e: initially failed due to test harness timing on CI workers, test adjusted and passed on second run; lint: pass; security-scan: pass. Overall: green after two reruns.
testing_notes: Added deterministic integration harness that simulates tenant-weighted pressure and regional capacity return. New tests cover: - transient thaw trigger window (10s default) - tenant_slo_weight gating - idempotent admin thaw endpoint under concurrent calls - atomic cache removal with backoff. Local perf run shows <0.5% p50 latency impact when controller is idle.
operator_guide_excerpt: Operators can trigger a transient thaw with POST /admin/circuit/thaw?tenant_id=<id>&reason=<text>. The endpoint requires operator token and will only thaw if tenant_slo_weight < 0.9 and no active global pressure flag is set. Thaw events are logged to audit stream and emit metric redwood.circuit.thaw.count with labels {tenant,initiator,reason} and trace id returned in response.
safety_and_rollout: Feature guarded behind feature flag runtime.transient_thaw (default enabled for canary region). Rollout: canary (us-west-2) -> tiered release across regions with 1-week observation. Metrics to watch: redwood.circuit.thaw.count, redwood.circuit.thaw.failures, route.5xx.rate, tenant.latency.p95. Quick rollback: toggle runtime.transient_thaw=false or PUT to /admin/feature/runtime.transient_thaw=false via operator console.
release_notes: Hotfix: reduce recovery time for tenants stuck in degraded circuits by introducing a transient thaw controller and operator thaw endpoint. Adds telemetry and safety checks to avoid reopen flapping. (ENG-19284, SUP-3456)
merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge. Commit message cleaned up to include core changelist and Linear reference. Post-merge: triggered canary rollout pipeline and staged metric alarms for thaw-failure spike. No incidents observed in canary over 48h.
postdeploy_observations: 48h canary: 12 transient thaw events triggered automatically (expected), 2 operator-invoked thaws, no increased 5xx rates, one thaw failure due to missing operator token (operator retried and succeeded). CPU and memory impact negligible. We observed faster tenant recovery times: median time-to-restore reduced from 150s to 18s in canary.
notes_for_followup: 1) Consider exposing a read-only per-tenant thaw history in console for postmortem workflows. 2) Investigate adaptive thaw window (auto-tune based on recent reopen flapping). 3) Add a rate-limit on operator-initiated thaws per minute to avoid accidental mass-thawing.
